newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end lower amid EMU jitters.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end lower amid EMU jitters.

text.p: Swedish shares closed lower on Monday after rising in early trade but slipping back amid worries over Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), with the crown losing ground, and Wall Street opening lower.
The Stockholm general index fell 1.04 percent to 2,735.75 after turnover of 3.29 billion crowns.
"It is very much the currency situation that is big now and worries about EMU," one broker said.
"It seems that no country qualifies any longer and it is putting pressure on its development. It was a really sad day today."
Bluechip shares close lower with telecoms group Ericsson down three at 269 crowns and drugs major Astra lost 6.5 to 360 crowns
The banking sector was in focus after Swedish holding company Lundbergs announced that it had sold its stake in Ostgota Enskilda Banken to Den Danske Bank.
Lundbergs closed four crowns higher at 133 and Ostgota Enskilda Banken gained 23.60 to 50.50 crowns, the price at which the shares were sold.
